title: WitnessCommon
description:
Shared definitions: evidence tiers, reason codes, and the source attribution block. Nothing here is a standalone document; it exists so tier and reason-code semantics have exactly one definition. SPEC.md sections 3 and 4 are normative for the meaning of these values; this file only constrains their shape.

FROZEN FOR MAJOR VERSION 1. Neither the tier enum nor the reason-code enum may lose or redefine a member. A tier whose meaning drifts retroactively falsifies every bundle already committed to a customer's git history, which is a failure mode with no recovery path.

tier.description:
Evidence tier. Answers exactly one question: if the party being audited is lying, what catches them?

A - attested. Produced by a runner under our control, journalled append-only, chain head anchored in git and pushed. Catches post-hoc edits of the journal.
B - host-attested. Independently retrievable from a third party the subject does not control. Catches local fabrication, but is perishable: once the host's retention window closes the claim can no longer be re-fetched.
C - self-reported. The agent said so about itself. Catches nothing on its own; git-anchoring makes it non-repudiable, which is a weaker and different property from verified.

Not a quality score and not a confidence level. See SPEC.md section 4.

reasonCode.description:
Why a field could not be filled. CLOSED LIST - an adapter may not invent a code; propose additions by PR.

host_does_not_emit - the host has no such concept, or exposes it on no surface.
host_gated - the surface exists but needs an entitlement this deployment lacks (e.g. GitHub Enterprise Managed Users).
not_yet_available - the surface is in preview and unstable.
permission_denied - credentials present but insufficient.
collection_failed - the surface was reachable but the read errored. MUST carry payload.error.
out_of_retention - the event predates the host's retention window.
not_applicable - the field is meaningless for this event kind.

The existence of this list is the point. An adapter that cannot fill a field emits null plus a code from here; it never omits the field and never substitutes zero, because a zero is indistinguishable from a genuine zero and turns a limit of the evidence into a false claim about it.

unavailable.description: Map of field path (JSON Pointer, relative to the containing document) to the reason that field is null. Every null field that a reader might otherwise expect to be populated MUST appear here. scripts/validate.sh and `witness verify` both check this coverage - a null with no reason is a defect, not an omission.

source.description: How this record was obtained. Mandatory on every observation: without it the tier is not computable and the bundle is invalid.

host.description: The system observed. Conventionally one of `github-agent-hq`, `github-actions`, `claude-code`, `codex`, `cursor`, `aidlc`, `witness-native`. Open-ended on purpose: a new agent host should be addable by writing an adapter, not by amending this schema.

channel.description: The specific surface the record came from: `enterprise-audit-log`, `rest-api`, `hook`, `otel`, `transcript`, `attestation`, `workflow-run`. Recorded separately from `host` because one host offers surfaces of different evidential worth - a GitHub attestation and a GitHub REST read are not the same kind of claim.

collected_at.description: When Witness obtained the record. Deliberately distinct from the event's own `timestamp`: the gap between them is how far behind the collector was running, which matters when a host's retention window is in play.

retrievable_from.description: Tier B only: a stable locator a verifier can re-fetch this claim from. MUST be null at tiers A and C, because at those tiers there is no third party to ask. This field is what makes `verify --online` possible.

adapter_version.description: Exact adapter build that produced the record, e.g. `claudecode/0.2.1`. Names what to re-run to reproduce.

then.$comment: A tier B claim that cannot be re-fetched is not host-attested; it is a tier C claim wearing a badge.
